form: In this paper, I argue that Hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ language is tensed, despite superficial evidence to the contrary. Even though Hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ is limited in overt tense morphology for present and past, every finite clause in the language contains some specific morphemes, which help to ground the utterance in space and time. These morphemes not only restrict the reference time to being non-future, but also illuminate specific temporal semantics of the utterances.

form: Halkomelem is a Central Salish language spoken in British Columbia, Canada. It comprises three major dialects: Halq'eméylem (the Upriver or Stóō dialect), Hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ (the Downriver dialect), and Hul’q’umi’num’ (the Island dialect). Hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, the focus of the present study, is an endangered dialect spoken on the Lower Mainland of British Columbia, whereas Hul’q’umi’num’ is spoken on southeastern Vancouver Island and the adjacent Gulf Islands.

form: In this example, the past tense morpheme appears three times: first, on the introducer clitic (nił [3rd person pronoun-EB] signals emphatic focus), second, on the verb (√c̓ew ‘help’), and third, on the subject NP (sil̓ə-s his grandparent). The first occurrence has scope over the main clause, the second occurrence has scope over the subordinate clause, and the third has scope over just the DP łə sil̓ə-s ‘his grandmother’, expressing a decessive meaning. Thus tense on nouns differs from tense on verbs — when cliticised to the predicate, the tense morpheme takes scope over the entire event; when cliticised to an NP, it only has scope over that entity (p. 20).

form: While Ritter and Wiltschko do provide evidence that spatial notions play an important role in interpreting Halkomelem clauses, they do not provide any convincing evidence that tense information is absent. For example, Matthewson (2006b) argues that there are obligatory temporal shifting effects in St’át’imcets embedded clauses, which crucially derive from the presence of a tense morpheme in the matrix clause […]. For a tenseless analysis to be convincing, we would either have to see that such temporal shifting effects are absent in Halkomelem, or that they can be re-analyzed successfully within a location-based system.
